---
title: "Getting Started"
---

## Welcome to the V2V Hub

Complete these six steps to set up your course workspace. **Time needed:** 30 to 45 minutes, most of it waiting on downloads.

:::{.callout-important}
## Before You Begin
Make sure you have a reliable internet connection and about 500 MB of free disk space.
:::

---

## Step 1: Create Your Workspace from the Template

1. Open the [course workspace template](https://github.com/AURA-Lab-SIUE/v2v-workspace) on GitHub
2. Click the green **Use this template** button, then **Create a new repository**
3. Name your copy (for example, `mc451-workspace`) and create it under your own GitHub account

This gives you your own copy of the course workspace on GitHub.

---

## Step 2: Install VS Code

1. Visit [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/)
2. Download VS Code for your operating system
3. Install and open VS Code

---

## Step 3: Install R, Quarto, and Git

Three more programs. R and Quarto are the two people most often miss, and Git is what lets you clone your workspace in Step 4. Install them in this order.

1. **R**, the language that runs your analysis: [Install R](resources/install-r.qmd)
2. **Quarto**, which turns your `.qmd` files into finished documents: [Install Quarto](resources/install-quarto.qmd)
3. **Git**, which tracks your work and copies the workspace to your computer: [Install Git](resources/github-setup.qmd#install-git)

:::{.callout-warning}
## Installing the VS Code extensions is not the same as installing these

VS Code has extensions named **R** and **Quarto**. They are front ends for the two programs
above. They do not install them, and having them is not the same as having R and Quarto on
your computer. You need both halves of each: the program, and the extension.
:::

**Verify:** close any open terminal, open a new one in VS Code (**Terminal, New Terminal**),
and run `quarto check`. Green check marks under **Quarto** and under **R** mean you are ready.

---

## Step 4: Open the Workspace in VS Code

Open the copy you made in Step 1 with the course picker: in VS Code, open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows/Linux, Cmd+Shift+P on Mac) and run **AURA: Open my course workspace**. Choose **Clone your copy from GitHub** (or open it if it is already on your computer), then trust the folder when VS Code asks, so R can run. For the full click path with screenshots, follow your course's guide: [MC 451](guides/mc451/02-open-your-course-workspace.md) or [MC 501](guides/mc501/02-open-your-course-workspace.md).

When VS Code prompts you to install the recommended extensions, accept them. They include:

- **Quarto**: authoring and rendering Quarto documents
- **R**: running and editing R code
- **AURA Lab R Companion**: a **Check my setup** command that installs the course packages and
  confirms they load, and an **Explain an R error** command

These are the front ends. If you skipped Step 3, install R and Quarto themselves now, or
the Render button will do nothing.

**Check your setup:** open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P, or Cmd+Shift+P on a Mac), run
**AURA: Check my setup**, and choose your course. It finds R, installs any course package that is
missing, confirms that each one loads, and checks the R extension, its sess helper, and the Quarto extension. `00-check-your-setup.qmd` runs the same check by hand.

---

## Step 5: Explore Your Workspace

Your workspace is organized into these folders:

| Folder | Purpose | What's Inside |
|--------|---------|---|
| **00_inbox** | Quick notes & ideas | Capture rough thoughts and discussion notes here |
| **01_journal** | Weekly reflections | Sample journal entries showing the three thinking paths (Connector, Troubleshooter, Critic) |
| **02_literature** | Reading notes & course materials | Includes textbook chapters and citation templates |
| **03_project** | Active research work | Organized by prospectus, codebook, data, and drafts folders |
| **04_resources** | Media & attachments | Images, PDFs, external files, and course materials |
| **_templates** | Reusable templates | The journal template (`_templates/journal-entry.md`) and a data dictionary template to copy and customize |

---

## Step 6: You're Ready!

Once you complete these steps, move to **[Phase I: The Journalist](modules/01_journalist/index.qmd)** to begin.

[Start Phase I →](modules/01_journalist/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg}

## Troubleshooting

**Q: VS Code won't open my workspace folder**
- Make sure you opened the folder you cloned in Step 4, not a parent folder
- Use **File > Open Folder** and select the cloned workspace folder directly

**Q: Where do I put my weekly journal entries?**
- Copy `_templates/journal-entry.md` into `01_journal`
- Rename the copy something like `week-01-yourname.md` and fill it out

**Q: Can I share my workspace with classmates?**
- Your workspace is yours; share the GitHub URL only when an assignment asks for it.

**Q: The install will not finish and I need R for class.**
- Open your own workspace copy as a Codespace: on github.com, open your repository, click **Code**, then **Codespaces**, then **Create codespace on main**.
- R, the course packages, and the R Companion are already installed there. Work in it, and bring the laptop to office hours
